Regulations Constitution of Brunei Darussalam (Order made under Article 83(3)) Free Trade Zones Order, 2014 Part I Preliminary Article 1 Citation, commencement and long title
(1) This Order may be cited as the Free Trade Zones Order, 2014 and shall come into operation on 1 January 2015.
(2) The long title of this Order is “An Order relating to the establishment of free trade zones in Brunei and to related and incidental matters”.
Article 2 Interpretation In this Order, unless the context otherwise requires— “activity” includes commercial and industrial activities and related operations;
“aircraft” means any machine that can derive support in the atmosphere from the reactions of the air and is capable of carrying passengers and goods by air;
“authority” means the person or body appointed under section 3;
“customs area” means any area outside a free trade zone;
“customs duty” has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Customs Order, 2006;
“dutiable goods” has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Customs Order, 2006 and the Excise Order, 2006;
“excise duty” has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Excise Order, 2006;
“free trade zone” means any area declared to be a free trade zone under section 4;
“goods” includes animals, plants and all kinds of movable property;
“manufacture” and its grammatical variations and cognate expressions mean the conversion of organic or inorganic materials by manual or mechanical means into a new product, and include the assembly of parts into a machine or other product, but do not include the installation of machinery or equipment for construction purposes, and such conversion is subject to the absolute discretion of the authority to determine whether any result of its manufacture is a new product or article;
“Minister” means the Minister of Finance;
“customs officer” has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Customs Order, 2006;
“value”, in relation to imported goods, means the value of the goods for the purpose of levying an ad valorem customs duty, including freight, insurance and all other charges, fees and expenses, but excluding any customs duty incidental to the purchase and delivery of such goods at the place of payment of duty;
“vehicle” means any means of conveyance other than an aircraft or a vessel;
“vessel” includes any ship, passenger boat or any other description of vessel used in navigation.
Part II Administration Article 3 Appointment of authority
(1) The Minister may, with the approval of His Majesty the Sultan and the Head of State, appoint any person or body as the authority responsible for the administration, maintenance and operation of any free trade zone declared under section 4.
(2) In addition to the powers provided by section 36, the Minister may in writing delegate any power or duty under this Order to an authorised officer.
Part III Free trade zones Article 4 Declaration of free trade zone Subject to any other written law, the Minister may, with the approval of His Majesty the Sultan and the Head of State by notification published in the Gazette, declare any area in Brunei to be a free trade zone, and such notification shall define the boundaries of the free trade zone.
Article 5 Exemption from customs duty Goods entering a free trade zone for any purpose permitted by or under this Order shall be exempt from customs duty and excise duty.
Part IV Operations permitted within a free trade zone Article 6 Control within a free trade zone A customs officer shall have power at any time to examine goods deposited in a free trade zone.
Article 7 Dealing with or disposal of goods within a free trade zone
(1) Any goods, other than goods expressly and absolutely prohibited by written law, may enter a free trade zone.
(2) Goods within a free trade zone may— (a) be removed from the free trade zone in their original packaging or otherwise, destroyed, or sent into the customs area or another free trade zone;
(b) unless the authority otherwise directs, be stored, sold, displayed, broken up, repacked, assembled, distributed, sorted, graded, cleaned, mixed or otherwise operated on or manufactured in accordance with this Order:
Provided that any goods sent from a free trade zone into the customs area which, on entry into the customs area, are liable to duty, whether in their original state or after manufacture, or as part of or an ingredient in goods manufactured for the free trade zone, shall be subject to the Customs Order, 2006, the Excise Order, 2006 and any regulations made thereunder.
(3) Under the Customs Order, 2006 and subject to subsection (4), goods transferred from the customs area into a free trade zone shall be treated as goods for export drawback.
(4) Section 2(b) shall not apply to goods which the Minister specifies by notification published in the Gazette, but such goods may be stored in a free trade zone for the purposes of transhipment or of measuring and repacking before being transferred into the customs area:
Provided that no such measuring and repacking shall be carried out without the prior permission of a customs officer and in accordance with such conditions as the customs officer considers appropriate to impose.
Article 8 Operations or manufacture
(1) No operation or manufacture shall be carried out in a free trade zone without the approval of the Minister, and that approval shall be published in the Gazette.
(2) A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence and, on conviction, shall be liable to a fine of not less than 20 times the customs duty or 100,000 Brunei dollars, whichever is the greater, and, in the case of a continuing offence, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years, or to both:
Provided that where the value of the goods cannot be ascertained, a fine not exceeding 100,000 Brunei dollars may be imposed.
Article 9 Operations or manufacture within a free trade zone
(1) A person who intends to assemble, mix or otherwise operate on goods for entry into the customs area, or to manufacture goods, in accordance with section 8, where the goods manufactured or the materials used are dutiable, shall give written notice of that intention to the authority and shall obtain approval. The authority may in its discretion grant or refuse the request:
Provided that, once approval is granted, the operation or manufacture shall be carried out under the supervision of a customs officer.
(2) Any operation or manufacture approved under this section shall comply with this Order and with such conditions as the authority considers appropriate to impose:
Provided that the authority may in its discretion grant an allowance for recoverable and non-recoverable waste, and where recoverable waste is sent into the customs area, customs duty shall be payable according to its condition, quantity and weight at the time of entry.
Article 10 Computation of customs duty
(1) The rate of customs duty and the valuation applicable to any dutiable goods (if any), where the goods lawfully enter a free trade zone or are manufactured within a free trade zone— (i) if no operation or manufacture resulting in a change of tariff classification has been carried out, shall be the rate and valuation in force on the date the goods enter the customs area;
(ii) if the goods are used in the manufacture of duty-free products entering the customs area, shall be the rate and valuation in force on the date the goods are transferred for manufacture; and (iii) if the goods are manufactured from duty-free materials, shall be the rate and valuation certified as in force by the relevant customs officer on the date the manufactured goods enter the customs area;
(b) if the goods are smuggled goods, shall be the rate and valuation in force on the date the goods became smuggled goods (if known) or on the date of seizure, whichever is the higher.
(2) The rate of exchange for determining the equivalent in Brunei currency of any foreign currency shall be the current selling rate in Brunei last notified before the goods are transferred for manufacture or enter the customs area.
(3) The valuation of any goods liable to customs duty and excise duty shall be determined under the Customs Order, 2006 and the Excise Order, 2006 respectively.
Part V Functions and powers of the authority Article 11 Facilities to be provided by the authority
(1) The authority shall provide and maintain within the free trade zone such facilities as are necessary to ensure the proper and efficient operation of the free trade zone.
(2) To ensure compliance with this Order and for the protection of revenue, the Minister may give the authority such directions as are necessary, and the authority shall comply with those directions.
(3) The authority shall permit the establishment of customs offices within the free trade zone and shall provide adequate facilities for customs officers performing duties in or around the free trade zone.
(4) The authority shall establish clear boundaries separating the free trade zone from the customs area in order to protect revenue, and shall make provision for persons, vehicles, vessels and goods entering and leaving the free trade zone.
Article 12 Authority may permit the construction of private buildings, etc.
(1) The authority may permit any person to erect such buildings and other structures within the free trade zone as may be required:
Provided that the authority may permit any person to erect buildings and other structures within the free trade zone on such terms as he may require.
(2) No such permission shall be granted where it would conflict with the normal use of the free trade zone.
(3) The authority may lease, or permit any person to acquire, hold or enjoy, within the free trade zone, movable and immovable property of all kinds, on such terms and for such period as the authority may determine.
Article 13 Exclusion or removal of goods
(1) Notwithstanding anything in this Order or in any regulations made under it, the authority may at any time and in its discretion, where it considers that the public interest, health or safety is endangered or prejudiced, order the exclusion or removal of any goods from a free trade zone, or the termination of any activity or service within a free trade zone.
(2) A person aggrieved by such an order may, under subsection (1), appeal to the Minister within 14 days after the order is served, and the decision of the Minister shall be final.
(3) An order under subsection (1) for the exclusion or removal of goods from a free trade zone shall, notwithstanding any appeal to the Minister, be carried out immediately, but an order for the termination of an activity or service shall not take effect until the outcome of the appeal supports the authority.
Part VI Financial provisions Article 14 Annual report and accounts
(1) The authority shall, within 6 months after the end of its financial year, submit to the Minister— (a) audited financial statements; and (b) a report on the work of the authority for the whole of the financial year.
(2) The Minister shall, on receipt of the financial statements and report, submit them to the Head of State.
Article 15 Accounts and records of transactions
(1) A person carrying on business or services within a free trade zone shall keep proper accounts and records of transactions and affairs in such form and manner, and for such period, as the authority may determine.
(2) Such persons shall submit accounts and records of transactions to the authority on demand.
(3) A person who contravenes subsection (1) or (2) commits an offence.
Article 16 Rates and fees
(1) Subject to this Order, the authority may set rates and fees for the use of premises or property belonging to or vested in the authority, and for the enjoyment of any service or facility provided by the authority.
(2) The authority may enter into agreements in respect of the matters referred to in subsection (1) without setting separate rates or fees.
Part VII Search, seizure and arrest Article 17 Search with warrant Where a magistrate, on complaint and after such inquiry as may be necessary, is satisfied that there is reasonable cause to believe that in any building, place, vehicle, vessel or aircraft within a free trade zone there are goods hidden or deposited, or that any activity is being carried on or service provided, in contravention of this Order or any other written law or any regulations made thereunder, the magistrate may issue a warrant authorising the customs officer named therein, acting alone or with assistance— (a) to break open any obstruction to his entry into or search of that building, place, vehicle, vessel or aircraft, or to seize and remove the goods under the authorisation;
(b) to enter and search the building, place, vehicle, vessel or aircraft where there is reason to believe that such an offence has been committed, and to seize any goods, and any document or other thing which may reasonably be believed to be connected with the case;
(c) to detain any person found in the building, place, vehicle, vessel or aircraft until the search thereof is completed; and (d) to arrest any person who is in the building, place, vehicle, vessel or aircraft, or who is found in possession of such goods, or whom the customs officer reasonably suspects of having hidden or deposited such goods or of carrying on such activity or providing such service.
Article 18 General power to stop and search
(1) A customs officer may, within a free trade zone, stop and search any vehicle, vessel or aircraft and anything carried therein, in order to ascertain whether the goods contained therein are in contravention of this Order or any other written law.
(2) The person in charge or in control of any vehicle, vessel or aircraft shall, on the demand of a customs officer, stop the vehicle, vessel or aircraft or move it to another place for inspection, and shall not proceed until permitted by the customs officer to do so.
(3) A customs officer may examine any goods entering or being removed from a free trade zone, and for the purpose of such examination may take the goods to a customs office and may open any container, package or receptacle.
Article 19 Search of persons Any person— (a) arriving or about to arrive at, or having recently arrived at, a free trade zone by vessel or aircraft, whether for the purpose of arrival or otherwise;
(b) entering or having recently entered a free trade zone by vehicle, or leaving or about to leave a free trade zone by vessel, aircraft or vehicle, shall, on the demand of a customs officer, either permit the customs officer to search his person, goods and baggage, or permit the officer to take away such goods and baggage, and permit the customs officer to search his person, goods and baggage forthwith:
Provided that— (i) no person who requires that his person be searched in the presence of a senior customs officer shall be searched unless that senior officer is present and supervises the search, and that person may be detained until that officer arrives or is brought to any office where that officer may be found;
(ii) no person who requires that he be present when his goods and baggage are searched, and who attends within a reasonable time, shall have his goods and baggage searched unless he is present; and (iii) out of respect for women, any woman shall be searched by another woman.
Article 20 Power of arrest and search
(1) Where any person is found committing or attempting to commit, or employing or assisting or abetting any other person to commit, an offence against this Order or any regulations made under it, a customs officer may, within a free trade zone and without warrant, arrest and search that person or cause him to be searched:
Provided that a woman shall be searched by another woman.
(2) A person arrested under subsection (1) shall be handed over to a police officer immediately and without unreasonable delay.
Article 21 Seizure
(1) All goods within a free trade zone— (a) which have been, or in respect of which there is reasonable cause to believe that they have been, dealt with in contravention of this Order or any other written law; or (b) which fail to comply with any condition of a licence, permit, approval or authorisation granted under any such written law, together with any container, receptacle, baggage, package, vehicle, vessel or aircraft which may be found to be carrying the goods or to be connected with the offence, contravention or breach, and any document or other thing which there is reasonable cause to believe is connected with the case, may be seized by a customs officer.
(2) All such goods, containers, receptacles, baggage, packages, vehicles, vessels and aircraft and the things carried therein shall, as far as practicable, be taken into the custody of the customs officer whose duty it is to receive them.
(3) Where any goods, container, receptacle, package, baggage, vehicle, vessel or aircraft and any thing found therein are seized under this Order, the officer making the seizure shall forthwith take reasonable steps to give notice of the fact of the seizure, in writing or otherwise, either personally or by post to the last known residence, to the owner:
Provided that no such notice shall be required where the seizure is made from the person himself, in the presence of the offender, or in the presence of the owner of the goods, container, receptacle, package, baggage, vehicle, vessel or aircraft or his agent, or in the presence of the master, pilot or person in charge of the vessel or aircraft, as the case may be.
Article 22 Return or disposal of movable property
(1) Where any movable property has been seized under this Order, a senior customs officer may in his discretion— (a) return the movable property temporarily to the owner or the person in possession, custody or control thereof, or to such other person as the officer considers entitled thereto, subject to such conditions as may be imposed and, in every case, on furnishing to the officer security sufficient to satisfy him that the movable property will be returned as required and will comply with the conditions (if any);
(b) return the movable property to the owner or the person in possession, custody or control thereof, or to such other person as the officer considers entitled thereto, who may freely dispose of the returned property, on furnishing security sufficient to satisfy the officer and not less than the amount required by the officer— (i) the open market value of the property on the date of its return; and (b) the taxes or duties payable under any written law, and, where the court orders forfeiture of that amount under section 23, the amount of the security shall be paid to the competent authority; or (c) where appropriate, sell or destroy the movable property, if it is a living creature, or if the officer considers it perishable or dangerous, or likely to diminish rapidly in quantity or depreciate rapidly in value, and the officer may hold the proceeds of sale pending the outcome of any prosecution or claim, and the proceeds shall be subject to the outcome of that prosecution or claim.
(2) A person who— (a) fails to return to a senior customs officer, as required, movable property temporarily returned to him under subsection (1)(a); or (b) fails to comply with or contravenes a condition imposed under subsection (1)(a), commits an offence and, on conviction, shall be liable to a fine of 40,000 Brunei dollars, or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years, or to both.
(3) For the purpose of exercising the powers conferred on a senior customs officer under subsection (1), the Minister may give to the authority such directions as he considers necessary or expedient, generally or in any particular case or class of cases.
Article 23 Forfeiture of goods
(1) All goods liable to seizure under this Order shall be liable to forfeiture.
(2) Any order for the forfeiture or release of goods liable to forfeiture under this Order shall be made by a court on a prosecution instituted in respect thereof, and where it is proved that an offence against this Order or any regulations made under it has been committed and that the goods were the subject matter of, and were used in the commission of, that offence, and the court is satisfied, the court may order forfeiture of the goods notwithstanding that no person has been convicted of the offence.
(3) The court may order forfeiture of— (a) in the case of goods returned under section 22(1)(b) but subsequently disposed of by the owner or the person to whom they were returned, the amount of the security under that subsection;
(b) in the case of goods sold under section 22(1)(c), the amount of the proceeds of sale, where it is proved that an offence against this Order or any regulations made under it has been committed and that the movable property (as the case may be) was the subject matter of, and was used in the commission of, that offence, and has been secured or sold and the court is satisfied, notwithstanding that no person has been convicted of the offence.
(4) All forfeited items shall be handed over to a customs officer and disposed of in accordance with the directions of the authority.
Article 24 Seizure of goods without prosecution
(1) Where no proceedings are instituted in respect of any goods seized under this Order, the goods shall be deemed forfeited on the expiry of one month from the date of seizure, unless a claim is made in the manner described below before that date.
(2) A person claiming to be the owner of such goods and that the goods are not liable to forfeiture may notify a senior customs officer of his claim, either personally or in writing through an authorised agent.
(3) On receipt of the notice, the senior customs officer may direct the release of the goods, or may refer the case, in such form as the Minister may determine, to a court having jurisdiction over the value of the claim.
(4) Where the court to which the case is referred has jurisdiction, the court may issue a summons to the person claiming to be the owner of the goods and to the person from whom the goods were seized requiring them to appear, and on their appearance or failure to appear, where it is proved that due service has been effected or attempted, the court may proceed with the hearing, and where the court finds that an offence against this Order has been committed and that the goods were the subject matter of, or were used in, that offence, the court may order forfeiture of the goods, or, in the absence of such proof, order their release.
Article 25 Return of seized goods to the owner or other person entitled The authority may order that goods seized under this Order (whether or not forfeited or deemed forfeited) be returned to the owner or other person entitled thereto on such conditions as it considers appropriate.
Part VIII Offences and penalties Article 26 Offences by bodies of persons, employees and agents
(1) Where a company, partnership, association or other body of persons commits an offence against this Order or any regulations made under it, any person who at the time of the commission of the offence was a director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of that company, association or other body of persons, a partner or manager of the partnership, or any person purporting to act in that capacity, or a person in charge or control of the company, partnership, association or other body of persons, shall be deemed to have committed the offence unless he proves that the offence was committed without his consent or connivance and that, having regard to the nature of his functions and all the circumstances, he exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of such an offence.
(2) Where any person is, under this Order or any regulations made under it and by reason of any act, omission, neglect or default, liable to the same penalty or forfeiture in respect of the act, omission, neglect or default of his officer, employee or agent, or of the officer or employee of his agent, but where the act, omission, neglect or default of the officer or employee occurred in the course of his employment, or was done by the agent while acting on behalf of that person, or by the employee of the agent in the course of his employment (in which case the agent shall be liable for the act, omission, neglect or default), his principal shall be liable under this section, Article 27 Penalty for offences not otherwise provided for Any act of commission or attempt in contravention of or non-compliance with this Order or any regulations made under it is an offence, and for an offence for which no penalty is expressly provided, the offender shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine of 1,500 Brunei dollars and, on a subsequent conviction, to a fine of 3,000 Brunei dollars, imprisonment for a term not exceeding 18 months, or both.
Article 28 Liability under other written laws Nothing in this Order shall be construed as exempting any person whose act, omission, neglect or default constitutes an offence under this Order or any regulations made under it from prosecution under any other written law, or from liability to any penalty or fine under any other written law that is higher than that under this Order or any regulations made under it, or to any penalty inconsistent with this Order or any regulations made under it.
Article 29 Entry into and remaining in a free trade zone
(1) No person shall enter or remain in a free trade zone without the permission of the authority, notwithstanding anything in this Order or any other written law.
(2) A person who enters or remains in a free trade zone shall comply with such conditions as the authority considers appropriate.
(3) A person who contravenes subsection (1) or (2) commits an offence.
Part IX Trial and proceedings Article 30 Person instituting prosecution No prosecution shall be instituted for an offence against this Order except with the written consent of the Public Prosecutor.
Article 31 Burden of proof Where in any proceedings against any goods seized for non-compliance with this Order or any regulations made under it, or otherwise forfeited, or for the recovery of any penalty or fine under this Order, a dispute arises as to whether the goods were lawfully entered or brought into a free trade zone, or lawfully operated on or manufactured, or lawfully used or consumed within a free trade zone, the burden of proof shall lie on the defendant in those proceedings.
Part X General Article 32 Appeals against decisions of the authority Where the authority has power to decide any matter under this Order or any regulations made under it, unless it is otherwise specially provided that the decision is at the discretion of the authority, any person aggrieved by the decision may appeal to the Minister, whose decision shall be final.
Article 33 Protection of the Government from liability The Government or the authority, as the case may be, shall not be liable for any loss suffered by reason of fire, theft, damage or any other cause while goods are in a customs warehouse or lawfully in the custody or control of a customs officer or an employee of the authority, unless the loss is caused by negligence, or by the default of a customs officer or an employee of the authority.
Article 34 Public officers Members of the authority and its employees shall, in the exercise of their functions or the performance of their duties under this Order, be deemed to be “public officers” for the purposes of the Penal Code (Chapter 22).
Article 35 Power of revocation The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, revoke any declaration or order made under this Order in respect of a free trade zone:
Provided that a decision under this section to revoke any order which has the effect of abolishing a declared free trade zone shall leave sufficient time for persons directly affected by the order within the free trade zone to make arrangements for the disposal of their goods.
Article 36 Regulations
(1) The Minister may, with the approval of the Head of State, make such regulations as are necessary or expedient for the carrying out and enforcement of this Order, including fees and other requirements or matters provided for under this Order, and for their proper administration.
(2) Such regulations may contain such incidental, consequential and supplementary provisions as the Minister considers necessary or expedient.
